title: Getting started with tallieR
text: ScoreMe can export participants one JSON file. Point read_scoreme() : read whole folder exports :
code: library(tallieR)  path <- system.file("extdata", "example_export.json", package = "tallieR") exp  <- read_scoreme(path) exp #> ℹ tallier_export: 2 participants | exported 2026-05-14T10:00:00.000Z study <- read_scoreme_dir("~/Downloads/my_study_exports/")

title: Getting started with tallieR
text: One row per participant, one column per questionnaire (recent session):
code: wide <- scores_wide(exp) wide[, c("code", "age", "sex", "ess", "isi")] #>   code age    sex ess isi #> 1 P001  28 female  10   5 #> 2 P002  45   male  20  22

title: Getting started with tallieR
text: One row per item response — useful reliability analysis IRT:
code: items <- items_long(exp) head(items[, c("code", "questionnaire_id", "item_id", "response")]) #>   code questionnaire_id item_id response #> 1 P001              ess    ess1        2 #> 2 P001              ess    ess2        1 #> 3 P001              ess    ess3        0 #> 4 P001              ess    ess4        3 #> 5 P001              ess    ess5        1 #> 6 P001              ess    ess6        0

title: Getting started with tallieR
text: tallieR rescores questionnaires raw item responses default. can also call scoring functions directly: PSQI returns named list component scores alongside global score:
code: score_questionnaire("ess", list(   ess1 = 2, ess2 = 1, ess3 = 0, ess4 = 3,   ess5 = 1, ess6 = 0, ess7 = 2, ess8 = 1 )) #> [1] 10  interpret_score("ess", 10) #> $label #> [1] "Excessive" #>  #> $color #> [1] "#EA580C" #>  #> $description #> [1] "Excessive daytime sleepiness. Consider clinical review." psqi_answers <- list(   psqi9 = 2, psqi2 = 35, psqi5a = 2, psqi4 = 5.5,   psqi1 = list(hour = 0, minute = 30),   psqi3 = list(hour = 7, minute = 0),   psqi5b=2, psqi5c=1, psqi5d=0, psqi5e=1,   psqi5f=0, psqi5g=1, psqi5h=1, psqi5i=0,   psqi6 = 1, psqi7 = 2, psqi8 = 2 ) score_questionnaire("psqi", psqi_answers) #> $global #> [1] 11 #>  #> $C1 #> [1] 2 #>  #> $C2 #> [1] 2 #>  #> $C3 #> [1] 2 #>  #> $C4 #> [1] 1 #>  #> $C5 #> [1] 1 #>  #> $C6 #> [1] 1 #>  #> $C7 #> [1] 2

title: tallieR — R tools for ScoreMe questionnaire data
text: Import score ScoreMe app questionnaire data R.  [!WARNING] tallieR early development formally tested. API may change without notice, scoring algorithms validated reference implementations, package undergone peer review. Use caution verify outputs independently using research context.

title: tallieR — R tools for ScoreMe questionnaire data
text: tallieR official R companion ScoreMe app. study session ends, ScoreMe exports participant data single JSON file. tallieR reads file — whole directory exports — re-scores every questionnaire raw item-level responses using algorithms embedded app, hands tidy data frames ready downstream analysis. designed work alongside slumbR: ScoreMe handles questionnaire side study, Sleep Diaries handles diary side, two R packages bring streams together R.

title: tallieR — R tools for ScoreMe questionnaire data
text: 📥 read_scoreme() — parse ScoreMe JSON export structured tallier_export object 📂 read_scoreme_dir() — batch-read whole directory exports tallier_study 📊 scores_wide() — one row per participant, one column per questionnaire (recent session) 📋 scores_long() — one row per participant × questionnaire × administration (full history retained) 🔬 items_long() — one row per item response, factor analysis, IRT, reliability checks 🧮 score_questionnaire() — re-score built-instrument raw answers list 💬 interpret_score() — return clinical score band (label, colour, description) score 📋 available_instruments() — list supported questionnaires IDs score ranges

title: tallieR — R tools for ScoreMe questionnaire data
text: Note MCTQ: score_questionnaire("mctq", answers) returns named list: msfsc (chronotype midpoint, decimal hours), sjl (social jetlag, hours), plus msw, msf, sd_w, sd_f. Expected answer keys: bt_w, sl_w, wt_w, bt_f, sl_f, wt_f (times {hour, minute} lists decimal hours; latencies numeric minutes), wd (workdays per week). Note PSQI: score_questionnaire("psqi", answers) returns named list global score seven component scores (C1–C7). Use result$global total access individual components directly. Note licensing: instruments require institutional permission research use. Please verify licensing requirements instrument use study.

code: library(tallieR)  # 1. Read one export file export <- read_scoreme("path/to/export.json")  # 2. Or read a whole directory of exports study  <- read_scoreme_dir("path/to/exports/")  # 3. Wide table: one row per participant × questionnaire session wide   <- scores_wide(study)  # 4. Long table: one row per participant × questionnaire × administration long   <- scores_long(study)  # 5. Item-level: one row per participant × questionnaire × item items  <- items_long(study)
